newsitem.title: USA: Ascend shares up on better-than-expected earnings.
newsitem.headline: Ascend shares up on better-than-expected earnings.

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc. shares jumped 8.9 percent Friday after the computer networking vendor reported fourth quarter earnings that were better than Wall Street expected.

Ascend, which makes the gear that controls the flow of information through computer networks, also hinted to investors that interest in its new products could boost revenue in coming quarters, analysts said.
Shares of Ascend, based in Alameda, Calif., rose $6.125 to $75 on Nasdaq trading of 8.2 million shares, making the stock the third-most active.

After the market closed Thursday, Ascend reported that net income for the fourth quarter more than doubled to $41.1 million, or 32 cents a share, from $13.5 million, or 11 cents, in the same quarter a year ago. Fourth-quarter revenue almost tripled to $177.5 million from $61.4 million.
Wall Street expected Ascend to earn 30 cents, according to a recent survey by First Call, an analyst tracking firm.

Ascend specialises in making telecommunication gear for Internet service providers and online services. Its equipment handles calls made by modems or high-speed telecommunication lines between remote offices.
Ascend told investors its revenue surged even though it cut prices on one of its product lines by 30 percent. The surge also came without the help of two much-anticipated products.
"We have been very successful in addressing the changing needs of our customer base," said Mory Ejabat, Ascend chief executive.
At least three analysts raised their rating on the stock and their earnings forecast for 1997 on Friday, based on expectations of strong sales of new and existing products.
